Ensemble

Your persistent agent team, inside OpenCode.

Ensemble gives you one group chat with named agents, a leader who routes the work, and a Work pane that shows what every agent is doing while each agent's native OpenCode session runs underneath. ```sh opencode plugin add @heyimteee/ensemble@0.1.1 ``` *The three-pane workspace in the synthetic Acme Notes fixture. The [documentation home](docs/README.md#see-it-in-motion) plays the short terminal replay of install, `/ensemble`, a group reply, the Work card, and the native session. Captures use synthetic data only; the install command is illustrative.* [Get started](docs/getting-started/README.md) · [What is Ensemble?](docs/getting-started/what-is-ensemble.md) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) ## What it does One OpenCode session is one conversation. Real work splits across research, review, implementation, and follow-up, so you copy context between sessions and lose track of who is doing what. Ensemble gives those agents one shared space: you talk to the group, the leader routes or answers, and every unit of work stays visible until it finishes. ### The three panes | Pane | What it shows | What you do there | |---|---|---| | Agents and workspaces | The roster grouped by workspace, plus a separate Workspaces list. New agents start with no workspace. | Select a workspace to open its group chat, or an agent to open a direct chat. | | Conversation | The group chat or direct chat, with the composer pinned below it. Replies stream in and settle into Markdown. | Send an unaddressed message to the leader, address a teammate with `$Name`, or reference a file with `@path`. | | Work | Work items for the current conversation in ACTIVE and HISTORY. `f` toggles the views. | Focus an item to inspect it, open its native session, or delegate, reassign, retry, restart, or cancel. | Below 118 columns the shell compacts; below 96 columns Work becomes a right drawer. The layout is tested from 80x24 up. ### What Ensemble is not - **Not a hosted service.** Everything runs in your OpenCode installation, with your providers and your files. Ensemble has no telemetry and uploads nothing. - **Not a model.** Agents use the models your OpenCode host reports; Ensemble does not ship one. - **Not a replacement for OpenCode.** Ensemble is one plugin inside the host. The native prompt, host commands, and OpenCode's permissions stay in charge. - **Not a permission system.** An approval in Ensemble is a team decision. It cannot override OpenCode's tool permissions. - **Not a Windows product.** Linux/tmux is the supported path in `0.1.x`; macOS with Herdr is verified on OpenCode 2.2.7; Windows is out of scope. ### What you get | Capability | What you get | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | Persistent team | Named agents with lasting instructions, models, backup models, skills, and memory. | You configure a teammate once and reuse it across projects. | | Leader routing | Unaddressed messages go to the workspace leader, who answers or delegates with a typed brief. | You do not repeat the same context to every agent. | | Visible work | Every turn and delegation appears as a work item with an honest state: QUEUED, WORKING, WAITING, RETRYING, NEEDS YOU, REPLIED, FAILED, STALLED, or CANCELLED. | You can see whether work is running, waiting on you, or actually broken. | | Native sessions | Each agent executes in its own OpenCode session; press `o` on a work item to inspect it. | You keep the host's tools, logs, and transcript instead of a black box. | | Bounded delegation | A dispatch budget caps a command, a group, and each delegation, and exhaustion is a controlled stop. | Multi-agent work cannot fan out without a ceiling. | | One team state | Roster, workspace membership, and bindings are shared across OpenCode locations. | The same team follows you between projects and terminals. | ### How the pieces connect ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Host["OpenCode TUI"] Rail["Agents and workspaces rail"] Chat["Group chat and composer"] Work["Work pane"] end Rail -->|"select a workspace"| Chat Chat -->|"unaddressed message"| Leader["Leader"] Leader -->|"answer"| Chat Leader -->|"delegate or hand off"| Work Work -->|"assignee runs the turn"| Native["Native OpenCode session"] Native -->|"reply and tool activity"| Chat Native -->|"status and result"| Work ``` ## Requirements Ensemble is one OpenCode plugin package, `@heyimteee/ensemble`, containing both the server and TUI parts. Compatibility is verified on OpenCode **2.2.6**, **2.2.7**, and **2.3.0** on Linux/tmux, with Node 22.23.4 or newer. The Node matrix runs on Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1; the live suites run on Node 26.12.1. The plugin peer range is `2.2.6 || 2.2.7 || 2.3.0`, and the workspace instruction block is contract v7. | Component | Supported | Notes | |---|---|---| | Linux with tmux | OpenCode 2.2.6, 2.2.7, and 2.3.0 | The supported path. Other terminals on Linux are untested. | | macOS with Herdr | OpenCode 2.2.7 | Installed path verified; macOS on 2.3.0 is not claimed. | | Windows | Out of scope | Native Windows and WSL are not tested. | | Node | 22.23.4 or newer | Older Node fails at plugin load with the supported range. | | Other OpenCode 2.x | Untested | The plugin loads with a runtime warning; behavior is not supported. | Read the [support matrix](docs/support/support-matrix.md) before installing on an unverified host. ## Install Install the stable release and confirm the plugin list entry: ```sh opencode plugin add @heyimteee/ensemble@0.1.1 opencode plugin list ``` ```text ensemble.v2 0.1.1 @heyimteee/ensemble@0.1.1 ``` Restart OpenCode, then open the workspace from the command palette or with `/ensemble`. Do not also load the same package from `.opencode/plugins/`; duplicate plugin IDs break the workspace. Do not use a Git spec (`github:`, `git+https://`, or `owner/repo#tag`) with OpenCode 2.2.7; Git dependency preparation fails upstream. Use the npm package or a local checkout path instead. The [install page](docs/getting-started/install.md) covers the single-plugin rule, a local checkout, and troubleshooting. To move from a prerelease, follow [upgrade](docs/getting-started/upgrade.md). ## Keyboard Ensemble starts in Normal and `Esc` never quits. Press `?` for the searchable catalog; it is the source of truth for every binding. | Key | Action | |---|---| | `i` | Focus the composer in Insert. | | `Enter` | Send in the composer, or open the focused row, result, or approval. | | `Shift+Enter` | Add a line in the composer. | | `Esc` | Go up one level. | | `Space` | Open the leader menu for create, edit, settings, approvals, and work actions. | | `:` | Open the command line with completion and history. | | `a` / `n` | From the rail, create an agent or a workspace. | | `e` | Edit the selected agent or workspace, including members and the leader. | | `f` | Toggle Work between ACTIVE and HISTORY. | | `o` | Open the focused work item's native session; on a group chat, choose a member. | | `d` / `t` / `r` / `R` / `x` | Delegate, reassign, retry, restart, or cancel the focused work item. | | `$Name` / `@path` | Address a teammate in the composer, or reference a workspace file. | | `F2` | Return to Ensemble from a native session. | ## Runtime diagnosis From a repository checkout, the doctor compares roster, workspace, membership, binding, and dispatch-ledger state across locations: ```sh npm run doctor -- /path/to/project /path/to/another-project npm run doctor -- --json --service-file /path/to/service.json /path/to/project ``` It exits `0` on agreement, `1` on divergence, and `2` on a usage, connection, snapshot, or config-read failure. It reads `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/service.json`, or `~/.local/state/opencode/service.json` when the variable is unset. Reports omit credentials, conversation text, and memories. A package-only install has no `npm` scripts; use the in-app `:logs` viewer and the host logs instead. See [data classes and retention](docs/privacy/data-and-retention.md). ## Support Ensemble is a developer preview. Support is best effort through GitHub Issues, with no paid support or SLA. Read the [support policy](docs/support/README.md) before filing. - Check the [support matrix and known limitations](docs/support/support-matrix.md) for the platform boundary. - Use the [incident runbook](docs/support/incident-runbook.md) for a broken workspace, stuck work, a failed upgrade, or suspected data loss. - Report vulnerabilities privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), never in a public issue. ## Known limitations - **Stable is `0.1.1`.** npm `latest` points at `0.1.1`; prereleases stay under `next` (`0.1.0-rc.3`). Pin the exact version for deliberate installs. This is a 0.x release, so minor versions may still change APIs. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). - **Host support is narrow.** Only OpenCode 2.2.6, 2.2.7, and 2.3.0 on Linux/tmux are tested. macOS/Herdr is verified on 2.2.7 only; Windows is out of scope. See the [support matrix](docs/support/support-matrix.md). - **Git-spec installs fail upstream on OpenCode 2.2.7.** Use npm, a loopback registry, or a local checkout. - **Diagnostics are local.** Ensemble has no telemetry and uploads no support bundle. The doctor ships in the repository, not in the package. - **Terminal accessibility depends on the host.** Ensemble supplies glyph-and-word status, reduced motion, `NO_COLOR`, and ASCII fallbacks; screen-reader output, high contrast, and copy-on-release are host features. - **Some surfaces stay native.** Arbitrary OpenCode slash commands are not proxied into the group chat, rich Markdown links are not clickable, and direct chats have no separate Ensemble search or export. ## Documentation - **Learn:** [what Ensemble is](docs/getting-started/what-is-ensemble.md), [install](docs/getting-started/install.md), [quickstart](docs/getting-started/quickstart.md), and [first team](docs/getting-started/first-team.md). - **Understand:** [Concepts](docs/concepts/README.md): agents, workspaces, routing, turns, work items, budgets, and native sessions. - **Do:** [Guides](docs/guides/README.md) and the [documentation home](docs/README.md). - **Look up:** [Reference](docs/reference/README.md): tools, commands, keyboard, configuration, environment, and supported hosts. - **Operate:** [Operations](docs/operations/README.md) for backup, restore, upgrade, and rollback. - **Assess:** [Security](docs/security/README.md) and [Privacy](docs/privacy/README.md). - **Contribute:** [Contributing](docs/contributing/README.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and the [evidence index](docs/contributing/evidence.md) for architecture decisions and verification records. - [Glossary](GLOSSARY.md), [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and [documentation style guide](docs/style-guide.md). ## License Ensemble is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Contributions are accepted under the same license.
